newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: STORK, METRA J/V SWD SEES 1997 GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: STORK, METRA J/V SWD SEES 1997 GROWTH.

text.p: Diesel engine maker Stork-Wartsila Diesel (SWD) said it expected to post strong growth in 1997.
"Based on the order book and sales in the first quarter of this year, SWD expects a rise of (1997) turnover to more than 600 million guilders," the company said in a statement.
SWD, a 60-40 joint venture of Finland's Wartsila Diesel and Dutch Stork , said it had won orders worth about 100 million guilders in the first quarter of 1997.
Last year, the company's sales rose by almost 17 percent to a record level of 509.3 million guilders.
Due to higher interest charges and costs of shifting production to a new site, the 1996 net profit (after tax) fell to one million guilders from a year-earlier 1.82 million.

Combining production facilities in the new plant, which will become operational in the second half of 1997, and good prospects of new products were expected to boost results in the years ahead. SWD said it had invested 30.4 million guilders last year to further develop two new diesel engines.
The recently announced merger between Wartsila Diesel and Switzerland's New Sulzer Diesel was also expected to strengthen SWD's market position, the Dutch group said.
